titulo: Present of -ar verbs, negation and questions: Regular verbs in -ar

aula.titulo: Present of -ar verbs, negation and questions
aula.objetivo: Conjugate regular verbs in «-ar» in the present, say what you do, where you live, work and study, make negative sentences and ask questions with «onde, o que, quem, quando» and «por que».

blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: Portuguese verbs are listed in the infinitive, and the infinitive tells you the family. Verbs ending in «-ar» (falar, morar, trabalhar…) are the largest family, and almost all of them are regular. STEP 2: to conjugate, remove «-ar» and add the ending for the person: eu fal-o, você fal-a, ele/ela fal-a, a gente fal-a, nós fal-amos, vocês fal-am, eles/elas fal-am. STEP 3: three forms are always the same: «você», «ele/ela» and «a gente» all take «-a». Only «nós» has «-amos». STEP 4: stress. In «falo, fala, falamos» the stress is on the stem («FA-lo»); in «falam» the ending «-am» is a weak nasal sound, like «FAH-lah~oo», and the stress stays on «FA». Do not stress the last syllable. STEP 5: the Portuguese present covers both the English simple present («I work here») and the English «-ing» form («I am working now»), so «Eu trabalho» can mean either. In lesson 17 you will meet «estar + gerund» for the «now» meaning. STEP 6: in many regions of Brazil, speakers who say «tu» use the form of «você»: «tu fala». Portugal uses «tu falas». The form «vós» is not used in everyday speech. STEP 7: the final «r» of infinitives is often very light in everyday speech, so «falar» can sound like «fala-ah». Write it correctly, though.
blocos.comparacao: In English the verb hardly changes: «I speak, you speak, we speak, they speak», only «he speaks» is different. In Portuguese each person has a different ending, so the subject is less necessary, although Brazilians use it more than speakers of Spanish. A big plus: English needs the helper «do/does» for questions and negatives («Do you speak? I don't speak»); Portuguese does not.

exemplos.ru: Eu falo inglês e um pouco de português.
exemplos.pt: I speak English and a little Portuguese.
Do you live in São Paulo?

erros.motivo: Do not use the infinitive after a subject: conjugate the verb.
«Vocês» is plural, so the ending is «-am».

erros.certo: A gente fala português. / Nós falamos português.
erros.motivo: «A gente» takes the «-a» form, like «ele/ela». You may hear «a gente falamos», but it is not standard.

blocos.enunciado: Say six sentences about yourself and people you know, with a different verb each time: «Eu moro em… Eu trabalho… Eu estudo… Ela cozinha… Nós viajamos… Eles falam…».
Say aloud: your name, where you are from, your nationality and your age. Then ask a friend the same four questions with «você» and then with «o senhor».
